newsitem.title: USA: NYC Water only gets $4 mln of retail bond orders.
newsitem.headline: NYC Water only gets $4 mln of retail bond orders.

text.p: The New York City Water Finance Authority on Friday said it received only about $4 million of retail bond orders in the first day of a presale period, as a two-point drop in Treasury bonds badly hurt demand.

An Authority official, who declined to be named, added that on Monday, he will meet with underwriters to decide whether the retail scale for the sale of up to $365.5 million of bonds will have to be repriced. "If the market is unchanged, we will look to see if it is appropriate to price yields upwards."

Despite Friday's big drop on two surprisingly strong economic reports --July payrolls and the National Association of Purchasing Management's overall index, which hit a two-and-a-half year high-- the Authority has no plans to scrap the sale.
"Oh no, the market's improved so much that even though this (fall) looks horrible, there's tremendous savings," the official said.
The precise size of the bond sale will be determined on Monday or Tuesday. The retail order period ends at 1500 EDT on Monday, and the bonds will be priced for institutional investors on Tuesday.

A senior vice president with Moody's Investors Service, Chris Evangel, said the agency would confirm the Authority's debt at A2, adding it also was giving the debt a positive outlook. The agency recently began attaching such outlooks, which reflect its view for the next 24 to 30 months, to its ratings.
